svg.title: Workflow for Cultivating Heedfulness & Skillful Qualities

g.text: Workflow for Cultivating Heedfulness & Skillful Qualities
This state is characterized by being "beset by birth, aging, & death; by sorrows, lamentations, pains, distresses, & despairs; beset by stress, overcome with stress" [AN_nblm.txt, 14, 15].
Do you desire to end suffering?
is described as a single quality that guards the mind and is reckoned as the foremost among all skillful qualities [AN_nblm.txt, 175, 176][KN_Iti_nblm.txt, 306][SN_nblm.txt, 502]. It involves being
, and cherishing it as one's highest wealth [AN_nblm.txt, 54][MN_nblm.txt, 393][KN_Dhp_nblm.txt, 302].
Developing mindfulness of death acutely for the sake of ending effluents [AN_nblm.txt, 111, 112].
Heedfulness requires abandoning misconduct and developing good conduct in these areas [AN_nblm.txt, 54, 55, 618].
Guard mind from passion, aversion, delusion, intoxication
Be mindful & alert in all daily activities (e.g., walking, standing, eating)

Heedfulness encompasses guarding mind-states, mindfulness in daily life, and a resolute pursuit of liberation [AN_nblm.txt, 55, 114][MN_nblm.txt, 380, 392, 394, 404, 455, 480][SN_nblm.txt, 552, 601][KN_Iti_nblm.txt, 309].
Live ardently & resolutely for ending effluents
are mental qualities and actions that lead to welfare and happiness, are blameless, and are praised by observant people [AN_nblm.txt, 2, 27, 614].
, hearing the True Dhamma, appropriate attention, and practicing the Dhamma [DN_nblm.txt, 244][SN_nblm.txt, 607].
in the Teacher's message, leading to hearing, remembering, penetrating meaning, pondering, desire, willingness, contemplation, and exertion [MN_nblm.txt, 430, 454].
, which help abandon passion and ignorance respectively [AN_nblm.txt, 3][DN_nblm.txt, 269][SN_nblm.txt, 565, 566].
The cultivation of skillful qualities involves a wide range of interconnected practices across conduct, mental states, and learning [1].
Practice Skillful Bodily Action (e.g., abstaining from taking life, stealing, sexual misconduct)
Practice Skillful Verbal Action (e.g., abstaining from lying, divisive/harsh speech, idle chatter)
Practice Skillful Mental Action (e.g., non-covetousness, goodwill, right view)
Develop Heightened Virtue (e.g., dwelling restrained by Pāṭimokkha rules)
Develop Heightened Concentration (Jhāna) (e.g., secluded from sensuality, entering meditative absorptions)
Develop Heightened Discernment (e.g., understanding arising/passing away, investigating truths)
Develop Mindfulness (e.g., the four establishings of mindfulness, in-&-out breathing)
Address Defilements (e.g., contemplation of unattractiveness for lust, goodwill for ill will)
Engage in Community & Learning (e.g., associating with admirable friends, listening to/discussing Dhamma)
Practice Generosity (e.g., being freely generous, openhanded)
Maintain Aroused Persistence (e.g., steadfast effort to abandon unskillful & take on skillful)
This directly results from cultivating skillful qualities [AN_nblm.txt, 36, 615].
Attain purity of mind, calm, & joy
This is the "liberation of the mind through lack of clinging or sustenance" [MN_nblm.txt, 421].
It is enabled by abandoning passion and ignorance [AN_nblm.txt, 4][DN_nblm.txt, 239].
Marked by the understanding that "Birth is ended, the holy life fulfilled, the task done. There is nothing further for this world." [MN_nblm.txt, 354].
"From the ending of craving is the cessation of stress" [AN_nblm.txt, 88][KN_Dhp_nblm.txt, 305].
This process leads to the purification of beings, overcoming sorrow, and realizing unbinding [DN_nblm.txt, 222][AN_nblm.txt, 61].
